meta.author: bank-team-integrated-3
meta.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.topic: The determinant and invertibility
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a matrix is invertible from its determinant
questions.stem: A software ticket asks whether matrix A with determinant 7 is invertible; what is the verdict?

options.text: No, because the determinant is not zero only for square matrices of odd order
Yes, because a nonzero determinant guarantees an inverse exists
No, because only identity matrices have inverses
Yes, because every square matrix has an inverse
options.misconception: assumes all square matrices are invertible

questions.explanation: A square matrix is invertible exactly when its determinant is nonzero. Here det is 7, so an inverse exists. Option D is wrong because singular matrices lack inverses.
questions.hint: Check whether the determinant is zero.

questions.topic: An eigenvalue computed from a characteristic polynomial
questions.learningObjective: Find an eigenvalue from a characteristic polynomial
questions.stem: For matrix B, the characteristic polynomial is lambda^2 - 5 lambda + 6; what is the smaller eigenvalue?
questions.explanation: Roots of lambda^2 - 5 lambda + 6 = 0 are 2 and 3, so the smaller eigenvalue is 2. The larger root 3 is the other eigenvalue.

questions.topic: A coordinate system in a stated basis
questions.learningObjective: Express a vector's coordinates in a given basis
questions.stem: In basis {u,v}, vector w = 3u - 2v; what is the second coordinate of w?
questions.explanation: Coordinates are the coefficients in the linear combination, so the second coordinate is -2. The first coordinate is 3.
questions.hint: Read the coefficient of the second basis vector.

questions.topic: A linear transformation and its matrix
questions.learningObjective: Identify the matrix of a linear map from its action
questions.stem: A ticket describes T(x,y)=(2x+y, x-y); which matrix represents T in standard basis?

options.misconception: sign error on the second row second entry

questions.explanation: Columns are images of basis vectors: T(e1)=(2,1), T(e2)=(1,-1), giving [[2,1],[1,-1]]. Option B has a sign error.
questions.hint: Compute T on e1 and e2.

questions.topic: A matrix representation under two bases
questions.learningObjective: Recognize when two matrices represent the same map
questions.stem: Two matrices represent the same linear map under different bases; what relation holds between them?

options.text: They are transposes of each other
They are similar via an invertible change-of-basis matrix

questions.explanation: Representations under different bases are similar: P^-1 A P. Determinant and eigenvalues are preserved, so D is wrong.

questions.topic: A Gram-Schmidt process
questions.learningObjective: State the first step of Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization
questions.stem: In Gram-Schmidt, given independent vectors v1,v2, what is the first orthonormal vector?

options.text: v1 minus its projection onto v2
v1 plus v2 divided by two

questions.explanation: Gram-Schmidt begins by normalizing the first vector: u1 = v1/||v1||. Starting with v2 or averaging is wrong.

questions.topic: A quadratic form and its matrix
questions.learningObjective: Extract the matrix of a quadratic form
questions.stem: For q(x,y)=2x^2+4xy+3y^2, what is the (1,2) entry of its symmetric matrix?
questions.explanation: The symmetric matrix has off-diagonal entries half the cross coefficient: 4/2=2. Diagonal entries are 2 and 3.

questions.topic: A vector space and its axioms in a concrete setting
questions.learningObjective: Test closure under scalar multiplication
questions.stem: The set of all 2x2 matrices with determinant 1 is tested for vector space axioms; which fails?
questions.explanation: Scaling a det-1 matrix by c gives determinant c^2, not 1, so scalar closure fails. Addition also fails but B is the listed failure.

questions.topic: A composition of linear transformations
questions.learningObjective: Compute the matrix of a composition
questions.stem: If T has matrix [[1,2],[0,1]] and S has [[1,0],[1,1]], what is the (2,1) entry of ST?

questions.topic: A basis and its dimension
questions.learningObjective: Find the dimension of a spanned subspace
questions.stem: Three vectors in R^3 are linearly independent; what is the dimension of their span?
questions.explanation: Independent vectors form a basis of their span, so dimension equals their count, 3. Dependent would reduce it.

questions.topic: A linear combination
questions.learningObjective: Decide if a vector is in a span
questions.stem: Ticket asks whether (1,2,3) is in span{(1,0,0),(0,1,0)}; what is the answer?

options.text: Yes, because the first two components match
No, because the third component cannot be produced
Yes, because any vector in R^3 is in the span
No, because the vectors are dependent

questions.explanation: The span has zero third component, so (1,2,3) is not in it. Option A ignores that constraint.

questions.topic: Linear independence
questions.learningObjective: Test a set for linear independence
questions.stem: Are vectors (1,0),(0,1),(1,1) in R^2 linearly independent?

options.text: Yes, three nonzero vectors are always independent
No, the third is the sum of the first two
Yes, because no vector is a scalar multiple of another
No, because two vectors span R^2

questions.explanation: (1,1) = (1,0)+(0,1), so the set is dependent. Option C misses combined dependence.
questions.hint: Look for a relation among all three.

questions.topic: An orthonormal basis
questions.learningObjective: Verify orthonormality of a set
questions.stem: Set {(1,0),(0,1)} is proposed as orthonormal under standard dot product; verdict?

options.text: No, they are not unit length
Yes, both unit length and mutually orthogonal

questions.explanation: Each has norm 1 and dot product 0, so orthonormal. No rescaling needed.

questions.topic: A symmetric matrix and the structure of its eigenvectors
questions.learningObjective: State eigenvector orthogonality for symmetric matrices
questions.stem: For a real symmetric matrix, eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are?
questions.explanation: The spectral theorem guarantees orthogonality for distinct eigenvalues of a real symmetric matrix.

questions.topic: A change of basis
questions.learningObjective: Compute a changed coordinate vector
questions.stem: Change-of-basis matrix P maps old to new; if old coords are (1,2) and P=[[1,0],[1,1]], what is new first coord?
questions.explanation: New coords = P^-1 old coords; P^-1=[[1,0],[-1,1]], so first coord = 1*1+0*2 = 1.

questions.topic: A positive definite matrix and what it implies
questions.learningObjective: Identify a positive definite matrix property
questions.stem: A symmetric matrix is positive definite; what can be said about its eigenvalues?

options.text: Eigenvalues can be any real number
At least one eigenvalue is zero

questions.explanation: Positive definite implies all eigenvalues > 0. Nonnegative allows zeros, which is semidefinite.

questions.topic: A least-squares projection onto a subspace
questions.learningObjective: Find the least-squares residual property
questions.stem: In least squares, the residual vector is orthogonal to which space?

options.text: The row space of the design matrix
The null space of the design matrix
The column space of the design matrix

questions.explanation: The normal equations make the residual orthogonal to the column space. Null space is unrelated.

questions.topic: A diagonalisation and what it simplifies
questions.learningObjective: State what diagonalization simplifies
questions.stem: A matrix is diagonalizable; what computation becomes trivial?
questions.explanation: If A=PDP^-1, then A^n = PD^nP^-1, so powers are easy. Determinant is also easy but A captures the main benefit.

questions.topic: A covariance matrix and what its entries are
questions.learningObjective: Interpret entries of a covariance matrix
questions.stem: In a covariance matrix, the diagonal entries represent?
questions.explanation: Diagonal entries are variances; off-diagonals are covariances. Correlations require normalization.

questions.topic: A principal component and what it maximises
questions.learningObjective: State what PCA's first component maximizes
questions.stem: The first principal component maximizes which quantity?
questions.explanation: PCA finds the direction maximizing projected variance. It is unsupervised, so labels are not used.

questions.topic: A projection onto the first component and the variance retained
questions.learningObjective: Compute variance retained by a projection
questions.stem: First component explains 80% of variance; projecting onto it retains what percent?
questions.explanation: Projecting onto the first principal component retains exactly its explained variance, 80%.

questions.topic: A claim about a model's structure that a determinant contradicts
questions.learningObjective: Use determinant to refute a structural claim
questions.stem: A ticket claims a 2x2 matrix with det 0 still has full column rank; locate the error.

options.text: The claim is correct; det 0 matrices can have full rank
Full column rank requires det nonzero for square matrices
Rank depends only on row count
det 0 means the matrix is zero

questions.explanation: For a square matrix, full rank is equivalent to nonzero determinant. det 0 means rank deficient, not zero matrix.

questions.topic: The spectral theorem stated for a real symmetric matrix
questions.learningObjective: State the spectral theorem conclusion
questions.stem: Spectral theorem for real symmetric A states A can be written as?

options.text: L U with L lower triangular
P D P^-1 with P arbitrary
Q Lambda Q^T with Q orthogonal
Q Lambda Q with Q not necessarily orthogonal

questions.explanation: Real symmetric matrices are orthogonally diagonalizable: A=Q Lambda Q^T. LU and arbitrary P are different decompositions.

questions.topic: A norm and the distance it measures
questions.learningObjective: Compute Euclidean distance from a norm
questions.stem: Vector u=(3,4) has Euclidean norm; what distance from origin?
questions.explanation: ||u|| = sqrt(3^2+4^2)=5. This is the Euclidean distance from the origin.

questions.topic: A span of vectors and the subspace it forms
questions.learningObjective: Describe the span of two non-collinear vectors in R^3
questions.stem: Span of two non-collinear vectors in R^3 is?
questions.explanation: Two independent vectors span a 2D subspace: a plane through the origin. Three would be needed for all of R^3.
questions.hint: Dimension equals number of independent vectors.

questions.topic: A repeated eigenvalue and its eigenvectors
questions.learningObjective: Describe eigenvectors for a repeated eigenvalue
questions.stem: A matrix has eigenvalue 2 with algebraic multiplicity 2; geometric multiplicity may be?
questions.explanation: Geometric multiplicity ranges from 1 to algebraic multiplicity. It is 2 if diagonalizable, 1 if defective.

questions.topic: An eigenvalue and an eigenvector
questions.learningObjective: Verify an eigenvector-eigenvalue pair
questions.stem: For A=[[2,0],[0,3]], is (1,0) an eigenvector, and if so eigenvalue?

options.text: No, it is not an eigenvector

questions.explanation: A(1,0)=(2,0)=2(1,0), so eigenvalue 2. Option B reads the other diagonal entry.

questions.topic: An eigenvalue computed from a characteristic polynomial
questions.learningObjective: Compute trace from eigenvalues
questions.stem: Eigenvalues of a 2x2 matrix are 4 and -1; what is the trace?
questions.explanation: Trace equals sum of eigenvalues: 4 + (-1) = 3. Determinant would be -4.

questions.topic: A linear combination
questions.learningObjective: Compute a linear combination of vectors
questions.stem: Compute 2*(1,3) - 3*(2,1); what is the first component?

questions.topic: Linear independence
questions.learningObjective: Count independent vectors in a set
questions.stem: Set has 4 vectors in R^3; at most how many can be linearly independent?
questions.explanation: Dimension of R^3 is 3, so at most 3 independent vectors. The fourth must be dependent.

questions.topic: An orthonormal basis
questions.learningObjective: Compute the norm of a unit vector after scaling
questions.stem: Vector v=(6,8) is scaled to unit length; what is the scaling factor 1/||v||?

questions.topic: A symmetric matrix and the structure of its eigenvectors
questions.learningObjective: Count orthogonal eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues
questions.stem: A 3x3 real symmetric matrix has 3 distinct eigenvalues; how many mutually orthogonal eigenvectors?
questions.explanation: Distinct eigenvalues of a symmetric matrix yield 3 mutually orthogonal eigenvectors, forming an orthonormal basis.

questions.topic: A change of basis
questions.learningObjective: Compute determinant of change-of-basis matrix
questions.stem: P=[[2,0],[0,3]] changes basis; what is det(P)?
questions.explanation: det(P)=2*3-0=6. The determinant of P scales volumes under the change of basis.

questions.topic: A positive definite matrix and what it implies
questions.learningObjective: Test positive definiteness via leading principal minors
questions.stem: By Sylvester's criterion, a symmetric matrix is positive definite iff?

options.text: All leading principal minors are positive

questions.explanation: Sylvester's criterion requires all leading principal minors positive. Positive entries or just det are insufficient.

questions.topic: A least-squares projection onto a subspace
questions.learningObjective: Compute the projection of a vector onto a line
questions.stem: Project b=(2,2) onto line spanned by a=(1,0); what is the first component of projection?
questions.explanation: proj = (b.a/a.a)a = (2/1)(1,0)=(2,0), first component 2.

questions.topic: A diagonalisation and what it simplifies
questions.learningObjective: Compute a matrix power via diagonalization
questions.stem: D=diag(2,3); what is the (1,1) entry of D^3?

questions.topic: A covariance matrix and what its entries are
questions.learningObjective: Compute covariance from centered data
questions.stem: Centered data products sum to 12 over n=4; what is the covariance?
questions.explanation: Covariance = sum of products / n = 12/4 = 3 (population). Sample would divide by 3.

questions.topic: A principal component and what it maximises
questions.learningObjective: Identify the constraint in PCA
questions.stem: In PCA, the loading vector is constrained to have?
questions.explanation: PCA loadings are unit vectors. Data is centered, but the loading constraint is unit norm.

questions.topic: A projection onto the first component and the variance retained
questions.learningObjective: Compare variance retained by one vs two components
questions.stem: First component retains 70%, second 20%; retaining both retains?
questions.explanation: Explained variances add for orthogonal components: 70+20=90%.

questions.topic: A claim about a model's structure that a determinant contradicts
questions.learningObjective: Refute invertibility claim using determinant
questions.stem: Ticket claims matrix with det 5 is singular; find the error.

options.text: det 5 means the matrix is zero
Singular means det zero, so det 5 contradicts

questions.explanation: Singular iff determinant is zero. det=5 means invertible, contradicting the claim.

questions.topic: The spectral theorem stated for a real symmetric matrix
questions.learningObjective: Apply spectral theorem to classify eigenvalues
questions.stem: Spectral theorem implies eigenvalues of a real symmetric matrix are?
questions.explanation: Real symmetric matrices have real eigenvalues. Complex pairs occur for non-symmetric real matrices.

questions.topic: A norm and the distance it measures
questions.learningObjective: Compute Manhattan distance
questions.stem: Manhattan distance between (1,2) and (4,6): what is it?

questions.topic: A span of vectors and the subspace it forms
questions.learningObjective: Determine span dimension from vector count
questions.stem: Two linearly independent vectors in R^4 span a subspace of dimension?
questions.explanation: Dimension of span equals number of independent vectors, so 2.

questions.topic: A repeated eigenvalue and its eigenvectors
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish algebraic and geometric multiplicity
questions.stem: Algebraic multiplicity of an eigenvalue is?

options.text: Its multiplicity as a root of the characteristic polynomial

questions.explanation: Algebraic multiplicity is root multiplicity in the characteristic polynomial; geometric is eigenspace dimension.

questions.topic: An eigenvalue and an eigenvector
questions.learningObjective: Compute an eigenvalue from Av = lambda v
questions.stem: A=[[4,0],[0,4]], v=(1,2); A v = ? times v, so eigenvalue?
questions.explanation: A is 4I, so every nonzero vector is an eigenvector with eigenvalue 4.

questions.topic: An eigenvalue computed from a characteristic polynomial
questions.learningObjective: Compute determinant from eigenvalues
questions.stem: Eigenvalues are 2 and 5 for a 2x2 matrix; what is the determinant?
questions.explanation: Determinant equals product of eigenvalues: 2*5=10.

questions.topic: A coordinate system in a stated basis
questions.learningObjective: Recover a vector from coordinates
questions.stem: Coordinates (2,-1) in basis {u=(1,0),v=(0,1)}; what is the vector's first component?
questions.explanation: Vector = 2u - v = (2,0)-(0,1)=(2,-1), first component 2.

questions.topic: A linear transformation and its matrix
questions.learningObjective: Apply a matrix to a vector
questions.stem: A=[[1,2],[3,4]] times (1,1); what is the first component?
questions.explanation: First component = 1*1+2*1=3. Second = 3*1+4*1=7.

questions.topic: A matrix representation under two bases
questions.learningObjective: Compute trace invariant under similarity
questions.stem: Similar matrices have the same?
questions.explanation: Similarity preserves trace, determinant, eigenvalues, rank, etc. Entries and column space need not match.

questions.topic: A Gram-Schmidt process
questions.learningObjective: Compute the projection subtracted in Gram-Schmidt
questions.stem: u1=(1,0); v2=(1,1); projection of v2 onto u1 is? (first component)
questions.explanation: proj = (v2.u1/u1.u1)u1 = 1*(1,0)=(1,0), first component 1.

questions.topic: A quadratic form and its matrix
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a quadratic form
questions.explanation: 1+2+1=4. This equals (x+y)^2.

questions.topic: A vector space and its axioms in a concrete setting
questions.learningObjective: Identify the zero vector in a function space
questions.stem: In the vector space of polynomials, the zero vector is?
questions.explanation: The zero polynomial acts as additive identity. Constant 1 is not zero.

questions.topic: A composition of linear transformations
questions.learningObjective: State dimension of composition of maps
questions.stem: If S:R^2->R^3 and T:R^3->R^2, composition T∘S maps?
questions.explanation: T∘S: domain of S (R^2) to codomain of T (R^2).
questions.hint: Domain of first, codomain of last.

questions.topic: A basis and its dimension
questions.learningObjective: Compute dimension of polynomial space degree <= n
questions.stem: Space of polynomials of degree at most 2 has dimension?
questions.explanation: Basis {1,x,x^2} has 3 elements, so dimension 3.

questions.topic: A linear combination
questions.learningObjective: Express zero vector as trivial combination
questions.stem: Linearly independent set has only which combination yielding zero?
questions.explanation: Independence means only the trivial (all-zero) combination gives zero. Nonzero coefficients imply dependence.

questions.topic: Linear independence
questions.learningObjective: Decide independence of a single vector
questions.stem: A single nonzero vector is always?
questions.explanation: A nonzero vector is independent. The zero vector alone is dependent.

questions.topic: An orthonormal basis
questions.learningObjective: State number of vectors in an orthonormal basis of R^n
questions.stem: An orthonormal basis of R^5 contains how many vectors?
questions.explanation: Any basis of R^5 has 5 vectors, orthonormal or not.

questions.topic: A symmetric matrix and the structure of its eigenvectors
questions.learningObjective: State that symmetric matrices are diagonalizable
questions.stem: Every real symmetric matrix is?
questions.explanation: Spectral theorem: real symmetric matrices are orthogonally diagonalizable, even with repeated eigenvalues.

questions.topic: A change of basis
questions.learningObjective: State that change-of-basis matrix must be invertible
questions.stem: A change-of-basis matrix must be?
questions.explanation: Any invertible matrix works as a change of basis. Orthogonal only if bases are orthonormal.

questions.topic: A positive definite matrix and what it implies
questions.learningObjective: State that positive definite implies invertible
questions.stem: Explain why a positive definite matrix must be invertible.

answer.exemplar: A positive definite matrix has all eigenvalues strictly positive, so zero is not an eigenvalue, hence the determinant is nonzero and the matrix is invertible.

questions.explanation: Positive definiteness gives strictly positive eigenvalues, so zero is not an eigenvalue and the determinant is nonzero, guaranteeing invertibility.
